1. The present suit and counter claim for damages have their origin in the alleged poor quality 'dhoklas' served by defendant no.1 which apparently have caused much grief to the plaintiff.

2 2. Vide this judgment, I shall decide the present present suit seeking recovery of damages under vicarious liability from the defendants as well as the counter claim filed by the defendant no.1 for recovery of damages against the plaintiff on account of defamation. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to by their position in the main suit titled 'Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh & Ors.'. 
PLAINT 3. The brief facts as mentioned in the plaint in the main suit are as under:
( i) The plaintiff is engaged in social work in the locality and worked as a freelance journalist before he was an electrician and doing electricity repair work in various houses and is sole bread earner of his family. 
Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh (ii) On 24.03.2019, the plaintiff visited Advocate Sh. Jai Prakash's office at C-7, Qutub Vihar,
Phase-1, Goyla Dairy, New Delhi - 110071 where one of his clients Sh. Sada Ram Kadian was present and Sh. Jai Prakash requested the plaintiff to go and purchase some sweets, dhokla and samosas for the purpose of eating with tea at about 10.30 AM. Plaintiff went to the shop of defendant no.1 and purchased barfee, samosas and  kg. Dhokla worth Rs.170/- and came back at the office of Sh. Jai Prakash. Plaintiff alongwith Sh. Sada Ram and Sh. Jai Prakash ate the dhokla and immediately fell unconscious. Thereafter, Sh. Jai Prakash and Sh. Sada Nand observed that the plaintiff's condition was serious and rushed him to nearby doctor (defendant no.2) and the doctor immediately prescribed some medicines and injection which were given to the plaintiff. 
(iii) The plaintiff's condition was very serious and when he regained consciousness, he called his family members and narrated the whole incident. Thereafter the plaintiff as well as Sh. Jai Prakash and Sh. Sada Ram found that the dhokla was smelling badly and they also notice a small bug,
creeping and crawling in the piece of dhokla. All of them immediately went to the shop of defendant no.1 and asked him that why he is selling Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh contaminated food on which defendant no.1 started shouting upon Sh. Jai Prakash and Sh. Sada Ram Kadian and called some of his relatives at the spot. 
The plaintiff requested defendant no.1 to issue a pucca bill but initially defendant no.1 did not do so but afterwards he gave the plaintiff a pucca bill after much pursuation. 
(iv) On the next day, Sh. Jai Prakash called the plaintiff to inquire about his health, on which he came to know that the plaintiff had swelling on his hip and was having severe pain and couldn't walk properly. On 25.03.2019, the plaintiff took second opinion from doctors of DTE of Health Service,
Govt. of Delhi who told that the plaintiff had eaten an virus-laden food and his health deteriorated due to infection. Therafter, the plaintiff went to defendant no.2 clinic and the doctor again Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
3 administered him injection for reducing pain but still the pain persisted. Defendant prescribed the medicines on a chit of paper and not on her letterhead. The plaintiff requested defendant no.2 for a proper prescription but she refused the same. 
(v) Thereafter, the plaintiff went to a doctor of Ram Manohar Lohia hospital where he was told that the pain was due to deficiency in service of the doctor i.e. defendant no.2. Since Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh 24.03.2019, the plaintiff has been running from pillar to post to take legal action against both the defendants and therefore, joint and vicarious liability was attracted against all the defendants. It is further averred that defendant no.3 i.e. Food Safety Department and defendant no.4 i.e. MCD are also liable as defendant no.1 was selling unsafe and unhygienic food. It is submitted that the Delhi Medical Council would also be liable for the negligence displayed by defendant no.2, who is registered and regulated by defendant no.5. 
(vi) All the defendants are liable for action against the unsafe food, whether by themselves or any other person on his behalf, manufactured or stored or sold and distributed and shall be punished for such failure or contravention. Due to the negligence of defendants, the plaintiff is claiming Rs.5,00,000/- for general damages for pain and suffering suffered by the plaintiff, and Rs.5,00,000/- as special damages for the incident that has been caused due to negligence of defendants to be paid jointly and vicariously by the defendants. 
Hence, the present suit. 
Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh WRITTEN STATEMENT, COUNTER - CLAIM,
REPLICATION, ADMISSION - DENIAL OF DOCUMENTS AND FRAMING OF ISSUES 4. A perusal of the Court file reveals that the suit was instituted on 07.06.2019 and summons were issued to the defendants. On 21.08.2019, defendants entered appearance through their counsels. On 02.11.2019, Written Statement was filed by defendant no.1 alongwith counter claim and letter dated 31.05.2019 of Mediation Centre addressed to Department of Law and Justice. Written Statement was also filed by defendants no.3 and 5 were filed on 27.09.2019 and 01.11.2019 respectively. 
5. In the Written Statement, the defendant no.1 has averred that the plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hands and suppressed material facts. It is also averred that the defendant no.1 went to attend Mediation against defendant no.1 without any evidence claimed Rs.80,000/- from defendant no.1 whereas the expenditure for his treatment is shown as Rs.1720/- and the present petition and claim amount has been increased to Rs.10,00,000/- and as such, the plaintiff is shifting his stand time and again. It is also averred that the plaintiff has falsely implicated defendant no.1 and the contentions raised in the plaint are false and frivolous. It is further averred that on the said date Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
4 Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh i.e. 24.03.2019 when the plaintiff had purchased dhokla from the shop of the defendant no.1, then it is obvious that dhokla was prepared in plenty numbers for sale in the market and it was sold to the prospective purchasers but none has reported it to be of inferior quality or that the same was injurious to health nor any such report is heard by defendant no.1 that after eating dhokla, any prospective purchaser suffered illness and food poisoning. It is further averred that the plaintiff created a scene on the shop of the defendant no.1 and spread rumours against him that the eatables of defendants are injurious for the public due to which defendant no.1 has suffered loss to his business and reputation, respect, image and his business and as such, the defendant no.1 has also filed a counter claim for recovery of Rs.5,00,000/- from the plaintiff.
6. Written statement to counter claim of defendant no.1 was also filed by the plaintiff. An application u/o VII R 11 CPC for rejection of plaint was also filed by ld. counsel for defendant no.1. 
In the Written Statements of defendants no.3 and 5, they have vehemently denied the allegations made by the plaintiff.
7. The counter claim filed by defendant no.1 against Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh the plaintiff was registered separately. 
8. On 16.03.2023, deficient court fees was filed by the plaintiff. On 01.02.2021, vide separate statement, application u/o VII R 11 CPC was withdrawn by the defendant no.1. On 01.06.2023,
status report was filed by defendant no.4/MCD. No Written Statement was filed by defendants no.2 and 4, hence their right to file Written Statement was closed and they are proceeded ex parte. 
9. On 01.06.2023, from the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed :
(I) Whether plaintiff is entitled to a decree of recovery of damages for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-, as prayed for? OPP. 
(II) Whether plaintiff is entitled to pendente lite and future interest at the rate of 18% per annum on the decreetal amount, as prayed for? OPP. 
(III) Relief.
10. In the counter claim, on 06.04.2021, on the basis of pleadings, the following issues were framed:
(I) Whether the counter claimant is Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh entitled for decree of recovery of damages of Rs.5,00,000/- in his favour and against defendant no.1, as prayed for? (OPCC) (II) Relief.
11. Thereafter, the matter was fixed for plaintiff's evidence. On 01.08.2022, in the counter claim it was ordered that the evidence led in the evidence led in the main suit be read as DE in the counter Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
5 claim. 
EVIDENCE LED BY THE PARTIES 12. On 21.09.2023, PW Sh. Jasvinder Singh was examined as PW-1. He tendered his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit Ex. PW-1/A. He relied upon the following documents :
(i) Original bill is Ex.PW-1/1 (colly) (OSR). 
(ii) Medical treatment provided to the plaintiff by defendant no.2 is Ex.PW-1/2 (colly). 
(iii) Photocopy of medical record is de-exhibited as Ex.PW-1/3 and is marked as Mark PW-1/3 (being photocopy) 
(iv) Photocopies of prescription is de-exhibited as Ex.PW-1/4 (colly) and marked as Mark B.
13. On 09.12.2023, PW-1 was cross examined wherein Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh he admitted that he had not made any complaint with the Food and Safety Department. He also admitted that he had not placed on record any written complaint to the Delhi Police with regard to the said incident. He also admitted that he did not send the sample of dhokla for testing. He also admitted that he did not give any complaint with respect to treatment administered by defendant no.2. He denied that the prescription of 28.03.2019 was of simple fever only and that he is falsely corroborating the incident of 24.03.2019. He also denied that he made cutting of date of 28.03.2019 to 24.03.2019 on Ex.PW-1/2. He further denied that suggestion that he has also made many other complaints against other persons to extract money and is a habitual litigator. He further denied that due to his wrongful actions, the plaintiff has suffered loss of reputation. 
14. Thereafter, vide separate statement of plaintiff, PE was closed and the matter was listed for DE. 
The defendant no.1 stated on oath that he did not wish to lead DE in the present suit. Defendants no.3 and 5 also stated on oath that they do not wish to lead DE. However, in the counter claim,
defendant no.1 has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A and relied upon General Trade / Storage License, GST Registration Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh Certificate and FSS License as Ex.PW-1/B (colly). 
15. In his cross examination, he has deposed that on 24.03.2019, PW-1 Sh. Bharat Singh deposed that he was present at the counter on the date of alleged incident i.e. 24.03.2019 when Sh. Jasvinder Singh/defendant came to purchase food items. He further deposed that the defendant never turned up at the shop after purchasing the articles. He further deposed that the articles sold by him were testified and verified by him and that no inspection was conducted of his food articles after the said Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
6 incident. He further admitted that MCD had issued a challan in 2021 due to non-renewal of trading license. He further deposed that the workmen who prepared the food articles were working with him for the last 2 years and are working even today. He further deposed that the food articles were packed in a proper manner. 
16. After the conclusion of trial, final arguments were heard on behalf of all the parties. On 23.04.2024, final arguments were concluded. 
CONTENTION OF PARTIES 17. Ld. counsel for the plaintiff submitted that it was an admitted fact that the plaintiff had purchased dhokla from the shop being run by defendant no.1. He submitted that the plaintiff Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh had been able to prove his case that as a result of eating the said dhokla, the plaintiff had suffered serious illness and thereafter, due to medical negligence of defendant no.2, had developed pain. He submitted that defendants no.3,4 and 5, who were responsible for regulating and controlling the services being provided by defendant no.1 and 2,
would also be liable vicariously for the poor and negligent services / goods provided by them. 
18. Per contra, ld. counsel for defendant no.1 submitted that due to the statements made by the plaintiff, the shop of the defendant no.1 which was well established for more than 20 years, had suffered loss of reputation. He has submitted that the suit filed by the plaintiff is a fishing expedition designed to extort money. He submitted that the plaintiff had earlier filed a claim of Rs.80,000/-
only before the Delhi Govt. Mediation and Conciliation Centre whereas he has filed a claim of Rs.10,00,000/- before this court. He submitted that the plaintiff has not come to the court with clean hands and his testimony is contradictory and unreliable. 
19. Ld. counsel appearing for MCD i.e. defendant no.4 and ld. counsel appearing for defendant no.5 made submissions on the same lines as ld. counsel for defendant no.1. Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh FINDINGS IN THE MAIN SUIT 20. The issues in the main suit shall be decided together. I find that the suit of the plaintiff has to be dismissed for the following reasons : 
(I) There is no corroborative scientific evidence to show that the dhokla sold by the defendant no.1 to the plaintiff was of a poor and adulterated quality, which could potentially cause any illness, as claimed by the plaintiff.
(II) The plaintiff has not been able to prove that the defendant no.1 was in the habit of selling poor and adulterated and unhygienic food or that any complaint had ever been made against them qua the poor quality of food to the relevant government Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
7 authorities. 
(III) The testimony of the plaintiff suffers from various contradictions and infirmities and can not be relied upon. During the cross examination, the plaintiff deposed that he had made complaint to the Delhi Police immediately after the incident but the police did not help him. It is pertinent to note that no such fact was ever mentioned in his evidence or in the plaint. No other evidence has been placed on record to show that the plaintiff made a 100 number call though the plaintiff has further deposed Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh in the cross examination that he did not make any complaint in writing but that the same was made verbally. It has not been explained as to whether the said verbal complaint was made in person at the concerned P.S. or through a 100 number call. 
As such, the said cross examination shakes the credibility and veracity of this witness. The plaintiff further states that he could not follow up his complaint with the Delhi Police as he was not well even though it is his story that after having recovered at the house of his advocate for two hours, he along with his advocate and one Sada Ram went to the shop of defendant no.1 to confront him. The said story does not ring true and appears to be false and fabricated . If the plaintiff was well enough to go to the shop of defendant no.1, then surely he would have been able to follow his complaint with Delhi Police, especially when he has also deposed that the Delhi Police, in fact, came at the time when he confronted the defendant no.1 at around 11.00 AM - 12.00 PM on 24.03.2019. The plaintiff has not attempted to produce any corroborative evidence to show the involvement of police. (IV) 
During the cross examination, the plaintiff also deposed that on the same day itself, when they went to confront defendant no.1 at his shop, the police was also called who came at the spot Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh and then threw away the remaining dhoklas. This testimony was in response to the cross examination conducted on behalf of defendant no.3 when he was asked as to why the remaining dhokla samples were not preserved so that they could be examined by the Food Adulteration Lab. This fact has cropped up in the cross examination for the first time and further damages the veracity of the plaintiff. If indeed the police had played such a role, then it is hard to believe that the plaintiff would have omitted to say so in his plaint. The plaintiff does not appear to be an illiterate or unaware person. He has impleaded not only the Food and Safety Department but also the Delhi Medical Council. He seems to be well aware about the role and functioning of the different authorities. If the Delhi Police had appeared at the spot and thrown away, what would be otherwise valuable evidence in the form of the remaining dhoklas, then the plaintiff would have surely raised a hue and cry about the same. 
(V) In his affidavit of evidence, it is narrated by the plaintiff that immediately on taking one small piece of dhokla, he lost consciousness whereas during his cross examination, he has deposed that he did not become unconscious immediately, but after 10 minutes. This again, is a material contradiction in his Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
8 Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh story. As per his story, after he became unconscious, he was rushed to the nearest doctor by Sh. Sada Ram and his advocate Jai Prakash. At this stage, a perusal of Ex.PW-1/2 which is the prescription issued by defendant no.2 would show that it is nowhere mentioned that the plaintiff i.e. the patient had been rendered unconscious. It has only been mentioned that he has complained of 'ghabrahat'. During the cross examination, the plaintiff had also deposed that after eating half piece of dhokla, he started feeling nauseous and after 10 minutes, he vomited. The fact of vomiting would naturally, in the ordinary course of events, have been mentioned before the doctor as he was examined soon after the incident as per the story put forward. It is unlikely that such fact would not have been mentioned by the said doctor. 
(VI) In this regard, it may also be mentioned that the plaintiff cast aspersions on the treatment given to him by defendant no.1 i.e. Dr. Sumitra. It is deposed by him that he approached a doctor at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, who informed him that the pain in his hip was due to the inefficient way in which he was given an injection by the defendant no.2. No such evidence has been produced by the plaintiff. The alleged doctor of Ram Manohar Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh Lohia Hospital has not been examined, nor has the prescription of the said doctor been duly proved. There is no evidence to show that in fact, the plaintiff as administered any injection by defendant no.2. The plaintiff has not even produced any medical expert who could depose about the injection given on the basis of the prescription given by Dr. Sumitra, which was exhibited as Ex.PW-1/2. 
(VII) In so far as the liability of defendants no.3,4 and 5 is concerned, it is apparent that there is no master-servant relationship between the Food and Safety Department / MCD and defendant no.1,
who is running a sweet shop. At most, they are market regulators but can not be made liable for any deficiency in service by the service providers regulated by them. They have no direction or control over the activities of the defendant no.1. Similarly, there is no master-servant relationship between the Delhi Medical Council and the defendant no.2 or for that matter, any other doctor who is a registered medical practitioner. The DMC is merely a regulatory authority, who can not be made liable for any alleged negligence by a particular doctor. Moreover, it has also come on record that the plaintiff did not make any complaint to defendant no.5 about the alleged Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh negligent service of defendant no.2. This further shows that the claim of the plaintiff is lacking bona fides. (VIII) The plaintiff has also not disclosed to the court that he had approached the Delhi Govt. Mediation and Conciliation Centre with his claim prior to filing the present suit. The same was first brought on record by the defendant no.1 and admitted by the plaintiff only during his cross examination that he had filed a case for Rs.80,000/- in the Delhi Govt. Mediation and Conciliation Centre against defendant no.1. The record of the Delhi Govt.
Mediation and Conciliation Centre and the complaint given by the plaintiff where entered into evidence Ex. PW-1/C. This fact further ensures that an adverse inference will have to be drawn against the plaintiff. In the complaint given by the plaintiff before the aforesaid Mediation Centre,
no mention is made that he had become unconscious. Rather, it is stated that the plaintiff had developed fever, vomiting, stomach ache and loose motions. The plaintiff has furthermore stated Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
9 that he could not work for 15 days and had to spend Rs.80,000/- for his treatment. The plaintiff has not proved even the expenses of Rs.80,000/-, let alone the sum of Rs.10,00,000/- claimed by him. 
There is not a single bill to show that a sum of Rs.80,000/- were spent on Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh medical treatment. 
(IX) No other witness has been produced to corroborate the story of the plaintiff. 
21. Therefore, the issues are decided against the plaintiff and in favour of defendant no.1. 
FINDINGS IN THE COUNTER CLAIM 22. The counter-claim has been filed on account of damages caused to the defendant no.1 due to the statements made by the plaintiff qua the quality of the dhoklas being sold by defendant no.1. It is claimed that the defendant no.1 has suffered loss to his reputation, respect and image in the locality of Qutub Vihar due to the publication made in the locality by the plaintiff qua the inferior quality of dhoklas being sold by defendant no.1. It is stated that defendant no.1 is conducting his business since more than 20 years and no such complaint has been received. On this account, damages are claimed. 
23. Before delving into the facts of the present case, it would be of benefit to recapitulate the law of defamation. In Prof. Imtiaz Ahmad v. Durdana Zamir 2009 SCC OnLine Del 477 : (2009) 109 DRJ 357 the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that:
Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh " ......Under law of defamation, the test of defamatory nature of a statement is its tendency to incite an adverse opinion or feeling of other persons towards the Plaintiff. A statement is to be judged by the standard of the ordinary, right thinking members of the society at the relevant time. 
The words must have resulted in the Plaintiff to be shunned or evaded or regarded with the feeling of hatred, contempt, ridicule, fear, dislike or dis- esteem or to convey an imputation to him or disparaging him or his office, profession, calling, trade or business. The defamation is a wrong done by a person to another's reputation. Since,
it is considered that a man's reputation, in a way, is his property and reputation may be considered to be more valuable than any other form of property. Reputation of a man primarily and basically is the opinion of friends, relatives, acquittance or general public about a man. It is his esteem in the eyes of others. The reputation spread by communication of thought and information from one to another. Where a person alleges that his reputation has been damaged, it only means he has been lowered in the eyes of right thinking persons of the society or his friends/relatives. It is not enough for a person to sue for words which merely injure his feeling or cause annoyance to him. Injury to feeling of a man cannot be made a basis for claiming of Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
10 damages on the ground of defamation. Thus, the words must be such which prejudice a man's reputation and are so Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. 
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh offensive so as to lower a man's dignity in the eyes of others. Insult in itself is not a cause of action for damages on the ground of defamation. 
8. Where the words are used without giving impression of an oblique meaning but the Plaintiff pleads an innuendo, asking the Court to read the words in a manner in which the Plaintiff himself understands it, the Plaintiff has to plead that the libel was understood by the readers with the knowledge of subject or extensive facts as was being understood by the Plaintiff." 
24. In Brig. B.C. Rana v. Ms. Seema Katoch & Ors 2012 SCC OnLine Del 5421 : (2013)
198 DLT 35, it was held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that:
"......As a principle of equity, every man is entitled to have his reputation preserved intact. A man's reputation is his property and possibly more valuable than other properties, and any words calculated to cause harm to his reputation affords a good cause of action. 
21. Odger says in his book on Defamation that "No man may disparage or destroy the reputation of another. Every man has a right to have his good name maintained unimpaired. Words which produce, in any given case, appreciable injury to the reputation of another are called defamatory, and defamatory words Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors. Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh if false are actionable."
22. In Miller v. Thompson 1874 LR 9 CP 118, attempt is made to define defamation as exposing a person to contempt, ridicule, or public hatred or to prejudice him in the way of office, profession or trade. 
23. Blackburn and George, in their Elements of Law of Torts, define defamation as a tort of publishing a statement which tends to bring a person into hatred, contempt or ridicule, or to lower his reputation in the eyes of right-thinking members of society generally, or which tends to make them shun or avoid that person. 
24. Faulks Committee in England in 1875 defines Defamation as "Defamation shall consist of the publication to the third party of matter which in all circumstances would be likely to affect a person adversely in the estimation of reasonable people generally." 
25. To claim that a particular statement is defamatory there should be publication to a third party and such publication should be of such a nature as is likely to cause appreciable injury to a person's reputation. Defamatory words, if false are actionable. False defamatory words, if written and Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh And Ors on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148097960/
11 published, constitute a libel, if spoken, a slander. In libel, the defamatory statement is made in some permanent and visible form in writing or otherwise recorded, such as, printing, typing, pictures,
photographs, caricatures, effigies. In Jasvinder Singh vs Bharat Singh and Ors.
Brij Sweets and Caterers vs Jasvinder Singh slander, the defamatory statement or representation is expressed by speech or its equivalents, that is, in some other transitory form, whether visible or audible, such as, a nod, wink, smile, hissing, the finger-language of the deaf and dumb, gestures or inarticulate but significant sounds. 
26. In an action for libel the plaintiff should prove that the statement complained of (1) refers to him; (2) is in writing, (3) is defamatory, and, (4) was published by the defendant to a third person or persons."
25. The present counter-claim fails for the reason that there are no pleadings or evidence to show that any defamatory statement has been published or spoken to third parties by the plaintiff. 
Moreover, the defendant no.1 has not pleaded regarding the exact statement and words published by the plaintiff. It is noteworthy that merely making such allegations in the suit filed before the court of law by the plaintiff would not constitute defamation. 
26. Therefore, the issues are decided against the defendant no.1 and in favour of the plaintiff.
